cards.b: Local area network: covers a small geographical area such as a building or school, owned by one organisation.
Wide area network: covers a large geographical area, often linking LANs, e.g. the internet.
Personal area network: a few metres around one person, e.g. phone and earbuds linked by Bluetooth.
Clients request services from a central server. Centralised management, backup and security, but the server is costly and a single point of failure.
All computers are equal and share their own resources. Cheap and no server needed, but harder to secure and back up.
A set of rules that allows devices to communicate, covering how data is formatted, sent and checked.
HTTP transfers web pages. HTTPS is HTTP with encryption, so data between browser and server is secure.
SMTP sends email. POP3 downloads email to your device. IMAP accesses email kept on the server and keeps devices in sync.
Source and destination IP addresses and a packet number so packets can be put back in order.
Data is split into packets that may take different routes and are reassembled in order at the destination.
A switch connects devices within a LAN and sends data to the intended device. A router connects different networks and directs packets.
IPv4: 32-bit, four denary numbers separated by dots. IPv6: 128-bit, hexadecimal groups. IPv6 gives far more addresses.
Domain name system: translates a domain name (www.example.com) into the IP address of the web server.
The internet is the global network of networks. The web is a service on it: web pages accessed by a browser using HTTP/HTTPS.

short.q: Give two advantages of connecting computers in a network.
short.model: Users can share files, printers and an internet connection. Data can be stored and backed up centrally, and users can communicate with each other.

short.q: State two advantages of wired connections over wireless connections.
short.model: Wired connections are usually faster and more stable. They are also more secure because data cannot be intercepted as easily without physical access.

short.q: Explain the role of a router in a home network.
short.model: The router connects the home LAN to the internet and directs packets between the devices and the outside network using IP addresses.
points: connects the LAN to the internet / other networks

short.q: Describe what happens when a browser requests www.example.com.
short.model: The browser asks a DNS server for the IP address of the domain name. It then connects to the web server at that IP address and requests the page using HTTP or HTTPS.
points: DNS translates domain name to IP address
browser requests the page from the web server using HTTP/HTTPS

short.q: Explain why mesh networks are more reliable than bus networks.
short.model: In a mesh, devices have many links so data can take another route if one link fails. In a bus, all devices share one cable, so a break in it stops the whole network.
points: mesh has multiple routes so one failure does not stop it
bus relies on a single backbone cable
